The Lucrative Shuttle Trade 

(first published on Sparta Market Outlook on 26 August - do subscribe to get the most up-to-date views)

1⃣The CEO of TotalEnergies said that there is a $10/bbl freight cost to do the shuttling of barrels from inside the Persian Gulf out to the Gulf of Oman. Total is reportedly one of the largest traders of oil from Iraq and Qatar.

2⃣The difference between the cost of a VLCC from Basrah to Ulsan, vs a VLCC from Fujairah to Ulsan is about $12/bbl. This sets the ceiling cost of bringing a cargo out from Basrah into the Gulf of Oman area, showing the reasonableness of the number quoted by Total.

3⃣SOMO sells Iraqi crudes on FOB basis, and the last Basrah Medium (BM) trade was at OSP - $25/bbl. 

4⃣From Sparta’s crude dashboard (snapshot taken on 26 August), the landed price of BM spot into the Far East is Oct Dubai – $2.30/bbl for a 20 September loader.

5⃣China reportedly bought BM at CFR Dubai + $10/bbl, implying the margin for the trader is ~$12/bbl. We have not counted additional war risk premium into this, which could erode the margin by another $4/bbl or so (assuming 5% at 80$/bbl)

6⃣We are seeing more Iraqi and Qatari barrels on offer now for October and November loading, which is showing that the shuttle trade is alive and well, and allowing more production to come back online from these Gulf producers.

7⃣ Kuwait also just announced they are in this trade. 

In the meantime, Asian refineries are now getting more options. So don't need to chase up the FOB premiums anymore.

US CENTCOM is saying that they escorted 750 million barrels of crude oil out over the past several months.

Maths again: Operation Project Freedom began 116 days ago on 2026-05-04, which is nearly 6.5 million barrels per day. That number most likely includes the brief MoU period, which saw twice as much traffic as now.

Here's an infographic we shared with clients a couple of days ago for folks to understand. The maths are quite simple.

Our method is to count the daily average of what departs the US Navy blockade line. We then substract from that what we know comes out of Oman and Fujairah. The rest is traffic deriving via the Strait of Hormuz.

Equation: USN - Oman - Fuj= SoH.

The Ship-to-Ship transfers happen in the Gulf of Oman west of the USN blockade line. Once the STS is done, the receiving party then departs via the USN blockade line. And that's where we count the regional departures.

That's the number that ulitimately moves oil markets.

https://t.co/chY9tBSS66 counts shipments to the global market when they pass through the US blockade line, monitoring the Automatic Identification System signals of ships because of restrictions on timely satellite imagery. On that basis, flows over the past seven days stand at just 3.7 million barrels a day, Samir Madani, the firm’s co-founder says.
